claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the open-world sandbox design, noting that the grappling hook, infinite parachute, and explosive destruction physics provide chaotic fun.

citations.review_text:
While far from perfect, Just Cause 2 is still worth a try to this day. The physics are slightly dated, but can lead to hilarious interactions and funny moments.

The game cranks up explosive action far more than Grand Theft Auto or even Saints Row, it's the definition of an action third person shooter.

1.1 hours on the counter. Looks like a game I hated.

Reality: it's a game that worked so fast it basically fired itself. One hour in, hook onto a car, parachute out, tether a guard to a passing truck, watch the ragdoll physics do something no scripted cutscene ever could, and my brain went "yeah, I need more of this, but bigger." So I bought Just Cause 3 on the spot and gave that one the hours it deserved.

Think of Just Cause 2 as the world's most effective free sample that I paid for. It didn't lose me. It graduated me. The DNA is all here, the grappling hook that turns physics into a toy, the explosions that are somehow the whole point, the sandbox that doesn't care what you do as long as you do it loudly. I left because the sequel does it louder, not because this one let me down.

Buy it cheap. Spend a night causing problems. Worst case, you also walk out wanting the sequel. That's a win either way.

The ultimate playground for pure, chaotic fun! 

Just Cause 2 is one of those rare games where the story doesn't really matter, because the gameplay is just an absolute blast. It is the definition of a perfect action sandbox. The combination of the grappling hook and the infinite parachute is pure genius. Once you master the physics of slingshotting yourself across the map, stealing fighter jets mid-air, and tethering enemy soldiers to gas canisters, modern traversal in other games just feels boring.

The open world of Panau is massive, gorgeous, and incredibly diverse. One minute you are driving a supercar through a neon-lit tropical city, the next you are snowboarding down a snowy mountain or raiding a military base in a dense jungle. The game constantly rewards you for causing "Chaos," which means your entire goal is to blow up fuel tanks, radio towers, and government property in the most spectacular ways possible.

The explosions look fantastic, the vehicle selection is huge, and the map scale is still impressive even today. It doesn't take itself seriously at all, and that's exactly why it works so well.

If you want a game where you can turn off your brain, perform insane Hollywood-style stunts, and blow up an entire island nation, Just Cause 2 is an absolute masterpiece of mindless fun.

Just reposting a review I did on GOG.

The version there seems more stable, so I decided to play it there.

Anyway, the game suffers from some problems on modern hardware, especially crashes caused by the decals. The solution is basically to disable them (they're not really necessary).

Just a heads-up.[hr][/hr]
[i][b]Big guns for such a small island.[/b][/i]

Many years have passed, and [i]Just Cause 2[/i] remains a beloved gem.

The game feels like a spiritual successor to the much-missed Mercenaries. And is part of a collection of action-based sandbox games that were very popular during the seventh generation.

It is the best gamification of the campy spectacles that were the action movies of the 80s. A complete indulgence, packed with one-liners.

The game features a modestly sized open map with competent presentation, packed with generic objectives that generally revolve around destroying something.

Practically everything is set up to explode. And you are strongly encouraged (and rewarded) to set the entire world on fire in order to accomplish your goals.

The game's universal unit is chaos. You destroy things to generate chaos, which in turn unlocks more opportunities to generate chaos. It's a self-perpetuating cycle.

One of the game's strongest features is its extremely fun traversal system, pairing a combination of vehicles of all kinds with an infinite parachute that you can activate at any time and a versatile grapple hook, which can be used to perform a variety of actions, from extending your glide to attaching enemy vehicles during a chase and making them whip around like toys. 

The result is navigation with a sense of freedom that was practically unmatched at the time, with plenty of room for skill-based maneuvers... and for intrusive thoughts to win.

I genuinely wasted far more time than I'd dare admit trying to hook a truck onto the blades of a wind turbine (didn't work).

Along with that comes a satisfying arsenal of weapons and explosives, ready…

claims.claim: Certain downloadable content (DLC) packages cause the game to crash on Steam Deck unless disabled.

citations.review_text:
First of all, I played this on a Steam Deck. If you're planning to do the same, make sure to disable the DLCs, otherwise the game will crash. The DLCs are purely cosmetic anyway.

Overall, I enjoyed Just Cause 2, even though the story is definitely not its strongest aspect. It was the perfect game to play for an hour in bed before going to sleep or during my train commute to work. Causing chaos to unlock more main story missions was fun. There are plenty of side activities to earn Chaos, and they're varied enough that unlocking the next story mission never really felt repetitive. I wouldn't recommend doing much more than this though. If you try to complete everything, the gameplay will start to wear thin quickly.

One thing that did bother me was the checkpoint system. The game only saves when you start or finish a mission. The "Save Game" option literally just saves your current checkpoint. That means if you spend time causing chaos in the open world and then die or quit, all that progress is gone. I eventually got into the habit of only stopping after starting or completing a mission, and fortunately there are plenty of missions, so it wasn't a huge issue. You can also just start en abort missions and trigger the checkpoint.

The destruction, gunplay, and overall chaos are where the game shines. The grappling hook is incredibly fun to experiment with. You can throw enemies off railings, pin pursuing vehicles to the road and watch them crash, ... Shooting also feels very accessible thanks to the very forgiving enemy hitboxes, making it a great game to casually pick up and play on controller.

I also found myself occasionally slowing down to take in the world. I'm not going to pretend it's the most detailed open world ever made, but standing on top of a mountain overlooking the landscape or cruising through the rivers and coastline genuinely transports you to Southeast Asia. In fact, I still have the game installed because I could see myself returning just to spend …

claims.claim: Reviewers report frequent random game crashes that interrupt gameplay progress.

citations.review_text: Don't buy this game. You're likely going to have the same issue that everyone else is having where the game crashes every twenty minutes. ♥♥♥♥ like this doesn't belong on steam if you literally CAN'T play it.

This is a life-changing game. It made me question my life decisions... Why did I think that playing this would be a good idea? Why did I sign up to get all the achievements?
The main story is super short and can be completed in 2 hours or so. But most of the time you'll be destroying same oil tanks, generators, statues and transformers in order to progress and unlock next story missions. And to put a cherry on top - there is an achievement for clearing the game to 75% (thank you that it's not 100%) and none of the destructible items or weapon / vehicle parts are marked on the map. This process is so tiring, boring and exhausting that I can't even describe...
The game tries to position itself as "go ahead and cause chaos. EXPLOSION! BOOM! CHAOS! ADRENALINE!", when in reality it's "haha. you missed a tiny transformer between those two building and a crate 100 meters from the main village. no 100% completion in this village for you sir, no".
Awful. Simply awful. It may be ok if you are trying to just complete the main game without getting all achievements. In that case - you'll probably need to clear out like 20 of the map, which is more bearable but still annoying. Otherwise - do not recommend.
Better play Just Cause 3. It's way better.

Special thanks to the graphics settings. Some of the graphics features were causing constant game crashes every 10 mins or so. So I had to turn off multiple settings just to make the game playable.
Maybe the worst game I have ever played. A lot of crashes happend to me and it a lot of bugs it has. I hope the 3rd part is more polished than this.

I remember when I was a little kid watching hours of modded multiplayer Just Cause 2 videos on YouTube. I always go back to those memories — especially the blimp in Mile High City where people would just hang out and talk about their lives. As a kid it felt like seeing what being an adult was like, with all the sins, alcohol, and everything else you didn’t fully understand yet but knew was there.

I was always curious about that mission where a Tesla coil or some kind of lightning shoots your fighter jet down over the island with Japanese soldiers. It looked so fun watching it, but when I finally did it myself it wasn’t as exciting. Still a nostalgic memory though. One thing I researched later was why the game uses the modern Japanese flag instead of the Imperial one — that was weird.
I originally had Just Cause 2 on Xbox but never finished it, so I bought it on PC recently to finally complete it. The versions feel literally identical. I did run into some issues on PC though — weird artifacts that would crash the game. I had to lower settings and do some research (even asked AI) to fix it. After that I haven’t had any crashes. The free roam, graphics, and how huge the world is still look amazing for how old the game is. The draw distance is insane.

The gameplay is exactly how I remembered — beautiful chaos. A lot of the open world stuff feels kinda useless compared to modern games, but back then it was awesome because you could just do whatever you wanted. I still want to try modding it and see how it runs on my computer now.
Oddly enough, the story felt pretty relatable to real-world situations like Iran. It made me feel like I was actually doing a regime change.

I definitely recommend picking it up if you haven’t played it.

I really wanted to enjoy Just Cause 2, but the experience ended up being more frustrating than fun. The gameplay has a lot of issues, especially with vehicle and bike controls, which often feel clunky and awkward. One of the worst parts is falling or gliding from high places — the camera becomes heavy and difficult to control, making many missions fail for reasons that don’t even feel like the player’s fault.

The crashes are another huge problem. Even with all game files installed correctly and a PC that can run the game easily, it still crashes randomly. It becomes extremely annoying when you barely finish a difficult mission, only for the game to close before it saves your progress. The game has fun ideas, but technical problems and frustrating controls ruin a lot of the experience.

I wanted to continue the "story" after completed Just Cause 1. This game has even less plot and possibly less interesting gameplay. Unfortunately the game would crash randomly very frequently so I was only able to complete about 30% of the missions/activities. It was a slog and I had intended to complete it, but the crashes were getting worse so I called it quits.

This game is not fun to play, frequent crashes for no reason, poor controls, sluggish aiming except when using mounted guns where its zips all over the place and ahrd to use, terrible driving and flying mechanics, awful story terrible characters. I cannot like this game even after finishing it, the game pads itself out by making you play god awful side missions which most of the time is just 'Kill this guy' , 'Liberate this base' or 'escort someone'. There are one or two cool missions but overall for me its not a fun experience, I was glad it was over when I finished the story. 3/10

citations.review_text: the only just cause game worth playing is 3. completion for this game sucks balls, its either running around a base or city looking for crates or driving slippery clunky cars in a race. this combined with the big open world makes the game even more repetitive.

Eeeeeh. Really hard time deciding on negative or positive with this one... but I did enjoy it overall, so I decided to stick with thumbs up:

This game is huge, tons of freedom, tons to collect, runs great (on deck too) and once you understand the progression system it can be kind of addicting. But it has a few fundamental flaws as well:

- This is a vehicle-game. You'll need them to travel, explore, do race events and destroy big military bases... But almost all of them handle like sht. Planes are very weird and don't have rudder controls, most helicopters are super heavy and slow, most cars feel like they're driving on ice even when not driving off-road and randomly lose control. I'm going to add "skydiving" to this category as well: I have no idea how that got through quality control. Free-falling events are nearly impossible to pull off, AND outside of events the game thinks you want to start skydiving ALL THE TIME when dropping from small ledges. So basically the controls can be very frustrating.

- The map is huge. But just having a huge map doesn't make a game fun. After a few hours you'll notice most pieces of base / settlement are copypasted and you might encounter an almost exact copy of it somewhere later. I realize reusing assets is basically required at this scale, but it still feels very diluted. There is not much more to find aside from the collectable crates and faction items, which are basically all the same in terms of finding them. 

There should have been some kind of score attack events, since it can feel very arcade-y sometimes. Obviously the story and acting are atrocious, but that never really was the point of this series I think. There also are quite some glitches and bugs that can occur. Gliding around with the parachute and grappling hook can feel kind of satisfying though.

Some fun can be had, just very diluted, and you'll encounter frustration.

Oh, Just Cause 2... One of my childhood games, with hundreds of hours played on the Xbox 360 back in the day. Might feel like a cheap GTA with a cliché story and clunky mechanics, but deep down it has a great gameplay and great scenario to explore and use as a playground.

The story takes Rico Rodriguez and the CIA to the fictional Asian island of Panau, having as mission to take down an agent and eliminate the dictator Baby Panay, with the help of three factions: the Reapers (a communist militia), the Roaches (the local mafia) and the Ular Boys (a religious-nationalist group). Honestly the story is pretty bland, but the missions are fun to play.

The gameplay is the best thing about the game, although it aged like milk in some aspects. The driving and flying feel too archaic despite being a 2010 game, having the sensation of driving just in straight line every vehicle. On the other hand, the glappling hook and parachute is way too satisfactly, being the most useful way to move around Panau. The combat sadly feels bitter-sweet, since yeah, you can be creative and use many weapons and the grappling hook to kill, but enemies are just bullets sponges in many cases. And I love Panau's map being so mixed, but the locations feel too repetitive. I'm not saying it's not fun, but you can see the years passed for Just Cause 2...

I have mixed feelings about the visuals. I love how Panau is so diverse having desert, jungles, a huge city, snowy mountains, forests... but the game nowadays looks kind of outdated. Yeah, it's a game released originally for Xbox 360 and PS3, back in 2010 (same year we got other games such as Fallout New Vegas, Red Dead Redemption, Alan Wake...), but I consider it the game that worse aged in graphics. 

In terms of OST and voice acting, I'd say the voice acting is weak, feeling like the voice actors were trying their best to put a Indian/Thai accent to the characters and a stupid Mexican accent to Rico, but the soundtrack is satisfying to listen to.

The game that made the franchise, Just Cause 2 still holds up today as one of the most fun sandboxes ever to be released; no wonder its developers are endlessly trying to recapture this lightning in a bottle. 

A lot can be said about what this game does right, but to me the main thrust is that Just Cause 2 truly gets what playing a sandbox should be like. The immense map, varied environments dotted with destructible enemy infrastructure and large collection of fragile vehicles means that your every journey will be a new experience, an odyssey of calamities wrought by you, the truly terrifying Rico Rodriguez. 

The game's story not only doesn't get in the way, but actively encourages this behaviour; the premise is that you're a CIA agent sent to a Southeast Asian island dictatorship with the sole goal of destabilizing it by wrecking as much stuff as possible; there are missions, but they're more like small challenges to get you to play the game in interesting ways and are often open enough as to not restrict your mindless fun.

The only exception are the faction mission, which are so standardised and run-of-the-mill as to feel like the developers put them in because they had to; like vegetables on your plate, they are the small unpleasantries which you must necessarily get past to enjoy an endless dessert of obliteration.

With the multiplayer mod bundled in for free, you really need to do yourself a favour and buy this game whenever you can - if you think you don't like sandboxes, this is the only true benchmark against which to test that belief.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the open world map features a large amount of copy-pasted and reused assets across settlements and bases.

citations.review_text:
A giant, antiquated turd with enough jank to rival the most notorious game releases in existence. It runs poorly, constantly crashes, you'll be fighting the camera and controls constantly, completing settlements accomplishes absolutely nothing as the three resistance factions will never get their sorry ass outside of the 9 bases you have to conquer for them. The world is completely empty, hopelessly outstretched and filled with nothing but constant copy-paste samey villages and military bases.

Playing through this earned me more frustration than pleasure, and I seriously do not understand how the fanbase prefers this game over JC3.

Eeeeeh. Really hard time deciding on negative or positive with this one... but I did enjoy it overall, so I decided to stick with thumbs up:

This game is huge, tons of freedom, tons to collect, runs great (on deck too) and once you understand the progression system it can be kind of addicting. But it has a few fundamental flaws as well:

- This is a vehicle-game. You'll need them to travel, explore, do race events and destroy big military bases... But almost all of them handle like sht. Planes are very weird and don't have rudder controls, most helicopters are super heavy and slow, most cars feel like they're driving on ice even when not driving off-road and randomly lose control. I'm going to add "skydiving" to this category as well: I have no idea how that got through quality control. Free-falling events are nearly impossible to pull off, AND outside of events the game thinks you want to start skydiving ALL THE TIME when dropping from small ledges. So basically the controls can be very frustrating.

- The map is huge. But just having a huge map doesn't make a game fun. After a few hours you'll notice most pieces of base / settlement are copypasted and you might encounter an almost exact copy of it somewhere later. I realize reusing assets is basically required at this scale, but it still feels very diluted. There is not much more to find aside from the collectable crates and faction items, which are basically all the same in terms of finding them. 

There should have been some kind of score attack events, since it can feel very arcade-y sometimes. Obviously the story and acting are atrocious, but that never really was the point of this series I think. There also are quite some glitches and bugs that can occur. Gliding around with the parachute and grappling hook can feel kind of satisfying though.

Some fun can be had, just very diluted, and you'll encounter frustration.

This game was seriously ahead of its time, and remains my favorite in the series. There is a lot of copy/paste asset re-use for bland bases to fill time post-completion, but the main story and sections are worth a playthrough.

Oh, Just Cause 2... One of my childhood games, with hundreds of hours played on the Xbox 360 back in the day. Might feel like a cheap GTA with a cliché story and clunky mechanics, but deep down it has a great gameplay and great scenario to explore and use as a playground.

The story takes Rico Rodriguez and the CIA to the fictional Asian island of Panau, having as mission to take down an agent and eliminate the dictator Baby Panay, with the help of three factions: the Reapers (a communist militia), the Roaches (the local mafia) and the Ular Boys (a religious-nationalist group). Honestly the story is pretty bland, but the missions are fun to play.

The gameplay is the best thing about the game, although it aged like milk in some aspects. The driving and flying feel too archaic despite being a 2010 game, having the sensation of driving just in straight line every vehicle. On the other hand, the glappling hook and parachute is way too satisfactly, being the most useful way to move around Panau. The combat sadly feels bitter-sweet, since yeah, you can be creative and use many weapons and the grappling hook to kill, but enemies are just bullets sponges in many cases. And I love Panau's map being so mixed, but the locations feel too repetitive. I'm not saying it's not fun, but you can see the years passed for Just Cause 2...

I have mixed feelings about the visuals. I love how Panau is so diverse having desert, jungles, a huge city, snowy mountains, forests... but the game nowadays looks kind of outdated. Yeah, it's a game released originally for Xbox 360 and PS3, back in 2010 (same year we got other games such as Fallout New Vegas, Red Dead Redemption, Alan Wake...), but I consider it the game that worse aged in graphics. 

In terms of OST and voice acting, I'd say the voice acting is weak, feeling like the voice actors were trying their best to put a Indian/Thai accent to the characters and a stupid Mexican accent to Rico, but the soundtrack is satisfying to listen to.

citations.review_text: The scale of the open world is incredible; fantastic sandbox.

I remember the anticipation around this game and looking at low quality screenshots with my friends. The sense of scale in this game is crazy, all these years later this 360 game still has one of the largest open world maps ever made.
Having such a gigantic map did hurt the game design a little but that didn't stop the game from being a fun sandbox to ♥♥♥♥ around in

PC port is old and often crashes though, i recommend looking up fixes before getting into this

Highly recommended! This game features a massive open world packed with things to explore and destroy. If you enjoy open-world action games with plenty of chaos and freedom, this is definitely one to check out.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game crashes frequently during play.

citations.review_text: Had to be careful of that mission with Karl right at the beginning. If like me you get stuck because Karl keeps blowing up. Just capture the enemy vehicle chasing Karl right before you get to the gas station. Solves the problem. Then...simply enjoy a PC classic. I have noticed like others that the game does crash from time to time.

How does one remain objective while judging one of those games that initially started their Steam account...

Well... unfortunately, by remaining objective and considering how constant crashing of the game really ruins the experience as the game exists as of today.
Seriously over 9 hours of game time to get the final achievements and 100% and every 15-20 minutes the game crashed and at one point after a crash, suddenly I was not able to even boot it up despite multiple reinstalls. 

I had to literally uninstall NVidia drivers and install them again, just so I can finish this game.


Despite this HUGE negative which is why I cannot recommend this title to newcomers as the 64bit systems seems to be fighting with this older game. 

There is still a lot of fun to be had,

The main storyline is not that long it's 5-6 missions tops. 
However as a sandbox it's a lot of fun, which will allow you to blow up a lot of things. 

I still have that one save file from back in 2010 where I have like 98% of the entire map finished with all the races, collectibles etc. 
Yet those were the days when a game would give you an experience like that... today it's more difficult to justify spending your time looking for crates and blowing up things.

If you are here after finishing Just Cause 1 then i would say its a better upgrade in every possible way. Combat, Game play and Story were great. I would have had lot of fun if it weren't crashing too often. There are fixes you can find it online but it will still crash though less frequently.

Huge map. You can cause chaos all over the places. Fun for those who likes to turn their brain off and blow things up.

3/5

[h1]At almost 1000 sq km, the map for this game is MASSIVE[/h1]

If you're a fan of open-world exploration, explosions, or both, chances are you already have this game. It's kind of like a B-movie, but the story is very short and is gated by a Chaos mechanic.

Story isn't the reason you play a game like this.

Rather, I play it for the satisfying explosions, funny physics, and the freedom to explore via parachute and grappling hook, or car, bike, boat, plane or even helicopter. I've played it 3 times now. Hard mode on PSN and PC, and more recently on casual on PC, and I love coming back to blow things the hell up.

__________________


A note on performance. I started out my casual run at 2560 resolution and most settings maxxed, but after a few hot weather days I found the game was crashing pretty regularly so I had to dumb things down. In hindsight, I think the game had similar problems the last time I played on PC, and it had crashing problems on PSN too. After a few tries at dumbing down various settings, I ended up with a semi-stable game that would run for a long time - but everything was on low, and most checks were off. I also ended up running 1920 in a window. All this after a re-installation as I had a problem with most buildings and enemies only loading as transparencies, and the grapple would not connect to them.

So when you start playing don't be fooled by how well it all seems to be going - it's worth dumbing everything down from the get go.

_______________


As fun as the game can be when things are going well and you find your rhythm, it isn't perfect. If you're in a helicopter and shoot and destroy one tiny object, you INSTANTLY get an attack chopper teleport in and start hammering your own aircraft with enemy fire. Regardless of difficulty, enemy numbers never seem to end in any sort of firefight either. As you progress, enemy alarm levels gradually upgrade to a maximum of 5, and you'll be surprised how fast it can fill up just by running around …

Just Cause 2 is maybe the most focused of any typical open-world game I've ever played. Blow stuff up. Great time.
The story is a decent parody of over-the-top action films. I'd say worth paying attention to for one play through. 
The grapple+parachute combo is great. The vehicles can feel sort of slippery at times, but a nice fast vehicle is fun.
The only big issue I have is the amount of glitches. Some are acceptable. Shooting someone making them go very high vertically was fun. The game crashing suddenly was less so.
Very much worth $15.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the open world map as massive and diverse, featuring varied biomes including urban areas, snow mountains, deserts, and jungles.

citations.review_text: First open-world game I played and I can't believe it's 15 years old. The map is huge and diverse, story was interesting too, as well as grappling and shooting mechanics. Still come back to it now and then for the nostalgia.

This game holds a special place in my heart. Back in the day I would push my poor and tired laptop to its limits trying to squeeze a playable FPS out of this game. I got about 300 hours out of it between the single and multiplayer mod. I do not at all remember what the story was, but I remember that the map, the vehicles, and the gameplay were endlessly exciting, keeping me coming back for more. The map itself is probably my favourite of any open world game, with an incredibly variety and diversity of terrain and biomes. From the urban jungle in the northwest, the snowy mountain villages in the east, to the sandy deserts in the south west, it allowed for an incredible amount of imagination, especially in the open ended multiplayer mod. I had hours upon hours of fun setting up scenarios with my brothers and friends, creating imaginary factions and wars, and pretending to take over the entire map through combined arms offensives. 

Whether in 2025 this game will have the same appeal and luster it had to 14 year old me way back when is up for debate. But for now I let this game hold a special place in my steam library as an underrated classic.

Hands down the best Just Cause entry in the franchise! I like this game so much that i have platinumed it in every platform (STEAM, PSN, Xbox).

The graphics are pretty good even in 2025, the map is huge and will take you forever to even get to 75% for the achievement and compare to Just Cause 3 it has two things that makes it superior to me: 1) Map and 2) Physics.

The map feels great - you have the same amount of desert, city, jungle and snow. In Just Cause 3 you have only cities that are "copy,paste", huge amounts of water areas and lot of empty mountains.

The physics feel more "natural" - idk how to describe it, but if you play both games you will notice it.

Fun fact: To this day, there's a bug in a mission which "softlocks" the game - In the mission "Death From Above" you have to destroy 3 fighter jets in a military base. If you destroy the 2 and you decide to drive the last one and instead of crushing it, you drive it up to the sky and jump out, the plane will get "stuck" in the air forever and will you have to restart the mission.

This is the best Just Cause game and the singleplayer game I've played the most. It may be a little dated now, both in terms of graphics and the effort required to get it to run without crashes, but it's well worth the effort. I played this game after playing JC3, and at first I didn't understand it. JC3 added a lot of polish and is definitely easier to play, but I'd still choose to play this one. There's something about how fast the game loads, how effortless it is to run on a modern PC, and how relaxing it is to explore the detailed world of Panau. This game has a much better map than the one note world of Medici. JC3 has a beautiful world, but it's only skin deep. JC2 took the time to add a gamut of environments, from villages and towns to cities and ports.

To those coming from Just Cause 3: give this one a chance...or a few. I thought the game made no sense and felt out of place, coming from JC3. But when I revisited the game again, I fell in love with the detail and the variety that this game offers, to the point that I'd trade my wingsuit and jetpack for the small details and easter eggs offered here. Think of how many distinct places you can recall from JC3. I can think of maybe five places that were truly distinct in that game. There's far more unique places in Panau, from the ski resort and capital city, to the military base with the gondola system and the rocket silo. All for a couple dollars on sale.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game gets repetitive, particularly when pursuing full completion, destroying identical military bases, or collecting scattered crates.

citations.review_text:
[h1]... MY NAME IS BOLO SANTOSI ...[/h1]

Just Cause 2 is a classic example of a game that mistakes vast, empty space for genuine depth, offering a map that feels less like a playground and more like a tedious chore list.

While the tropical island of Panau is undoubtedly impressive in sheer size, traversing it becomes a mundane exercise in frustration as you spend the vast majority of your playtime flying, driving, or grappling over unremarkable terrain that hides the same repetitive military bases behind every corner. The core gameplay loop is mind-numbingly circular: you glide into a base, blow up the exact same red-colored fuel tanks or radar dishes you’ve destroyed a hundred times before, watch the chaos meter tick up, and move on to the next identical objective without ever feeling like your actions have any meaningful impact on the world. The narrative is an insult to the medium, presenting a script so painfully cheesy and voice acting so wooden that you’ll find yourself skipping every cutscene just to stop the embarrassment, especially when your protagonist, Rico Rodriguez, spouts lines that sound like they were rejected from a budget 80s action flick.

The controls are equally problematic, particularly when it comes to the clunky vehicle handling that makes steering a car feel like trying to maneuver a boat through molasses on an ice rink, and the aiming system, which suffers from a jittery inconsistency that turns even basic firefights into a war against the camera and the reticle.

[h1]... OUUUUUUUUUCH! ...[/h1]

Yet, in a bizarre concession to the game’s design, there is an undeniably juvenile "joy" to be found in its absurdity; tethering a panicked soldier to the back of a speeding jet or launching a propane tank into a group of enemies and watching the physics engine succumb to total, rag-doll madness provides a fleeting surge of entertainment that keeps you hooked just long enough to realize how empty the rest of the experience truly is. i got this game again and played it to 100% completion because this is a childhood game for me. despite that, i don't think i could recommend it to others though simply because just cause 3 is a better experience in movement, appearance, sandbox experience, and more. and yet i still had some fun. it gets repetitive very fast though, so i would only recommend destroying enough settlements to finish the story, and then stop.

please do not 100% this game. for many reasons. it's an incredibly repetitive 100 hour experience, and i even ran into a unresolvable bug on the mission black gold and had to start over.

A fantastic sequel to the original game, improving upon it in almost every way. Gorgeous and reasonably varied locations to explore with lots of intriguing POI, versatile gameplay (within the boundaries of explosive sandbox mayhem it aims to deliver, cutting out stealthy approach of more seriously toned competitors the likes of Far Cry series), over-the-top satirical B-movie story, grappling hook galore, insane amount of vehicles and myriads of content. That said it doesn't come without flaws and jank which becomes increasingly more noticeable as the game grows old - especially in terms of enemy AI and eventual repetitiveness. After all, zooming around exotic island nation destroying property and killing goons of an unhinged dictator, with the occasional race challenges and the like in the mix, can only stay same amount of fun for so long. But it was long enough for me to complete every single achievement in the game and then some, so what gives? All in all, a silly high-octane classic that delivers kind of sandbox experience we don't get to see much - moreso well executed - today. "Bye-bye Baby!"
COULD NEVER FINISH IT, BACK FOR ANOTHER GO EVEN THOUGH ITS QUITE REPETETIVE

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the combination of the grappling hook and parachute as a core mechanic enabling fluid movement and traversal across the map.

citations.review_text:
At a time when the most vertical open-world games I’d played were [PROTOTYPE] and Assassin's Creed II, Just Cause 2 felt like someone had suddenly ripped the ceiling off what traversal could be.  Pairing the grappling hook with the parachute was pure flow-state energy - once you got into that rhythm of launch, glide, swing, repeat, the entire island became a playground.  It wasn’t just traversal, it was a vibe, and it made the usual downtime of going from the end of mission A to the start of mission B feel genuinely fun.

This game also holds a special place as the first title I ever hundo’d on Steam. If memory serves, the achievements only ask for 75% completion, but I kept going until I was hovering in the 99-point-something range before learning two locations were glitched.  Even then, I didn’t regret my time.  I was blowing stuff up and collecting upgrades because I wanted to.

The formula has been refined in later games and across the industry as a whole, sure, but there’s a raw charm to Just Cause 2’s chaos and movement that still makes it easy to recommend.

Fun for nearly all ages.  My father and I both played the hell out of this one on both X360 and PC.  Great driving, flying, and boating physics.  Lots of guns, and the infinite parachute opens up a lot of mobility options.  You'll find a lot of opportunities for emergent gameplay with this one.

It's getting a bit old, but if you're into the genre and haven't played this one, I bet it holds up pretty well.

citations.review_text:
100% COMPLETION IS STILL IMPOSSIBLE WITHOUT A MOD DUE TO A GLITCH WHERE COLLECTABLES AND A WATER TOWER DO NOT SPAWN.

The harder difficulties which is required for 100% has no proper balancing, the enemies are just made into bullet sponges and have perfect aim, the enemies with shotguns even become snipers, even able to hit me while flying in a helicopter. 

There are also over a thousand collectables in the form of boxes scattered all of the map that takes days and days to get them all. 

Also the races suck in this game, the planes are basically impossible to turn which makes the plane races difficult and the base jumps are actually impossible due to the lack of movement while falling through the air and the camera which spins like crazy when falling.
But note  you need to download  2 files to get 100% completion. They can be found on the internet.
